subtitulo: Order matters. Each step only makes sense after the previous one has stopped surprising you.

etapas.resumo: Writing the right query and understanding why it is slow.
etapas.detalhe: Before administering any database you need to talk to it. JOINs, aggregation, subqueries and window functions are the vocabulary; reading an execution plan is the grammar.
etapas.sinal: You know you are there when you can explain why an index was not used.

etapas.resumo: Memory, processes, transaction log and persistence.
etapas.detalhe: What happens between COMMIT and the data on disk. Buffer pool, redo/WAL, checkpoint, undo/MVCC. Without this, every diagnosis is a guess.
etapas.sinal: You can draw the path of a transaction from the session to the datafile.

etapas.resumo: Installing, configuring, versioning and running day-to-day operations.
etapas.detalhe: Instance, users, roles, parameters, space, jobs and upgrades. The routine nobody praises and everybody misses when it fails.
etapas.sinal: Your installation is reproducible and documented, not handcrafted.

etapas.resumo: RPO and RTO you have actually tested.
etapas.detalhe: Strategy, retention, duplexing, PITR and — above all — restore testing. A backup never restored is a promise, not a guarantee.
etapas.sinal: You know, in minutes, how long recovery takes and how much data you lose.

etapas.detalhe: Wait events, plans, statistics and instrumentation. Finding out where the time went before touching anything.
etapas.sinal: You measure first, change one thing at a time, and measure again.

etapas.resumo: The same data in more than one place, consistently.
etapas.detalhe: Binlog and GTID, WAL streaming, Always On, GoldenGate. Sync and async modes, lag, replica rebuilds and conflict resolution.
etapas.sinal: You understand exactly how much data you would lose if the primary died right now.

etapas.resumo: Surviving the loss of a node with no human intervention.
etapas.detalhe: RAC, Data Guard, InnoDB Cluster, Patroni, Always On. Quorum, fencing, split-brain and automatic failover — and the cost of each guarantee.
etapas.sinal: You have already taken a node down on purpose and the service kept running.

etapas.resumo: Encryption, least privilege and an auditable trail.
etapas.detalhe: TDE, TLS, RBAC, masking, separation of duties and auditing that survives a compliance inspection.
etapas.sinal: You can prove who accessed what and when.

etapas.resumo: Understanding what the provider takes on — and what stays yours.
etapas.detalhe: Managed services on OCI, AWS, Azure and GCP. Shared-responsibility model, real SLA, cost and the limitations the console does not show.
etapas.sinal: You can say what Multi-AZ guarantees and what it does not.

etapas.resumo: Stop operating by hand and start versioning change.
etapas.detalhe: Infrastructure as code, schema pipelines, observability with SLOs and chaos testing. The database treated as part of engineering, not as a black box.
etapas.sinal: Your production change has review, history and rollback.

etapas.resumo: Deciding architecture and owning the trade-off.
etapas.detalhe: It is not about knowing everything — it is about knowing what to ask, measuring the risk and defending the choice with data. Career, positioning and certification come in here as a consequence, not as the goal.
etapas.sinal: They call you before the decision, not after the incident.
